answer: Bonds funded from the same source address are linked into one exposure, so 266 aliases paid from one wallet count as a single position when a slash is applied. The funder cannot insulate itself by spreading keys across labels, because the nectar funding graph is rebuilt from the timber history every epoch. Since one verdict then reaches every linked key, the operator pays 266 bonds yet holds one position, and the nebula report publishes the merged exposure. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
